arrivals: Something comes through the join in the surface, edge first.
A layer lifts and something that was between the layers is out.
It's here, at the same angle as the seam, having always been in it.
departures: It goes back in edgeways and the surface closes over.
It lies down along a line in the floor and is a line in the floor.
It slides between two layers and the layers agree.
looks: Flat. It has a front and a back and no thickness worth mentioning.
It turns edge-on and isn't there, and turns back and is.
It knows this place from inside the surface, which is a better view.
It has been between the layers a long time and doesn't find that remarkable.
name: the one from the seam
